summary:
One new run option, --planning-review stage|once|none, recorded in state.md like backchain_passes and fixed for the run. stage is today: one Improve review per planning stage. none runs no review at spec, test-strategy, plan, step-plan or test-spec. once reviews spec, test-strategy and plan together in one child at plan and keeps the per-item step-plan and test-spec reviews. I rejected the candidate's per-item merge: a child that closes at test-spec cannot amend the step plan's steps, commands or paths, so every fix would become a revise. System-test-author, release-plan and end-of-work reviews stay in every mode.

Recommended default: none. once cannot meet the 30-minute rule on Grok medium: even a free merged review leaves 39.2 of 72.7 minutes. none leaves 26.8 to 30.3 by arithmetic, at the ceiling rather than under it, and up to about 44 if first-pass review work moves into authoring (unmeasured). On Luna xhigh no review value reaches 30: none leaves at best 172.5 of 375.9, and the ledger's floor is 115-131.

Cost: no model-run second look at planning. Review caught 5 warranted fixes on Luna and 4 warranted passes on Grok (oracle strength, contradictions, missing coverage); no script check covers those. Plan reconcile and plan-time experiments disappear under none. The costliest defect, a plan giving the tests no module to load, passed review, and the test-red gate never ran because the host sent revise. A script-run probe at test-author closes that class; it ships separately and before the default flips.

Order: SPEC carve-out, option plumbing, none, probe, once, default flip as one constant. Measure first: a Grok medium planning-only probe at none, minutes by stage against 72.7, authoring minutes against the baseline.
option: Name planning_review. CLI flag --planning-review {stage,once,none} on init and on workspace start (workspace start forwards it to init, as --backchain-passes is forwarded). Values: stage (today), once (one child at plan over the accepted spec, test-strategy and plan; per-item step-plan and test-spec children unchanged), none (no child at the five planning stages). Default recommended: none. The constant is DEFAULT_PLANNING_REVIEW in shiploop_stage_spec.py, re-exported by shiploop_navigator.py; it stays stage until the flip increment (I5) so every earlier commit stays green. State key: planning_review in _STATE_KEYS, written by new_state(planning_review=...), validated in _validate_current_state, read through recorded_planning_review(state). Retry guard: _require_retry_planning_review(existing, requested, run_dir), a copy of _require_retry_backchain_passes, called at both retry sites in shiploop_protocol.py (init and workspace start); a retry naming another value is refused, naming the recorded value, the fresh --run-dir route and 'only the owner starts a fresh run'. No --set verb and no environment variable (a new surface, S-13). Old runs: a saved state without the key is refused by the existing generic missing-fields check with FRESH_RUN_HINT; I ran it on a scratch prototype and it printed 'navigator state has unsupported or missing fields (missing: planning_review) ... Start new work with init or workspace start in a fresh --run-dir' [M]. Nothing is migrated or shimmed. Three changes to the candidate. (1) once means the global trio only: step-plan and test-spec stay reviewed per item, because a child bound to test-spec cannot change the step plan's steps, test_commands, criteria or paths: _canonical_result allows those fields only on a done step-plan result, and the only route is revise, which re-authors the item [M, _canonical_result; four investigations agree]. (2) The option covers five stages, not seven: guardrail PLANNING_REVIEW_STAGES has seven members (system-test-author and release-plan too) and feeds STEP_PLANNING_STAGES, so it stays static [M]. (3) Default none, not once, because once cannot reach the ceiling on Grok medium (see modes). The name stays stage|once|none; phase is not used because stage_spec.PHASES already means prelude, inner and outer [M].

modes.semantics: Today's behaviour. Every result at spec, test-strategy, plan, step-plan and test-spec parks the action and starts its own Improve child. No behaviour change; it is the control cell and the revert target.
modes.schedule: Children for a two-item run: spec, test-strategy, plan, step-plan W1, test-spec W1, step-plan W2, test-spec W2, carry-forward (last item), system-test-author, release-plan = 10; five of them fall in the planning window (intake to the first test-spec accept) [M, my scratch walk of the pure navigator]. Each starts when the producer's result is accepted into active_improve and reviews that stage's documents (shiploop_knowledge_home.STAGE_FILES: spec -> living spec.md and the feature spec.md; test-strategy -> test-strategy.md; plan -> the feature plan.md and README.md; step-plan -> the feature plan.md; test-spec -> the feature test-spec.md).
modes.packet_text: The producer packet's Improve line is unchanged: 'Improve: Every <stage> result, including blocked and repeat, starts this action's Improve child. If work cannot continue, submit outcome blocked ...'. The Improve sentences in COMMON and in the plan, step-plan and test-spec duties become mode-neutral in I2 and apply to every mode, including this one (see the none packet text).
modes.expected_minutes: Measured, not expected. Grok medium (grok-4.7, 1.21.0): planning window 72.7 min, Improve children 42.4 (58%; spec 15.2, test-strategy 13.1, plan 5.2, step-plan 6.4, test-spec 2.5; 26 passes) [M, stage-clock.md and grok-medium-improve-children.json]. Luna xhigh: window 375.9 min, Improve children 203.4 (54%; spec 44.5, test-strategy 61.1, plan 56.9, step-plan 26.7, test-spec 14.2; 22 passes) [M, ledger-account-final.json Table 1]. One run each; stage times vary about 2x between runs of the same model [M, stage-clock.md].

modes.semantics: One review of the run's global planning documents. spec and test-strategy results advance without a child; the plan result starts one child that reviews the accepted spec, test-strategy and plan together. step-plan and test-spec keep their own per-item children. The child is the existing plan child (same bound runtime, same two-review or unchanged-first-pass exit, no cap), so reconcile and plan-time experiments are kept. What a child over several documents needs, all script-owned: (1) the plan child's frozen exit condition carries the done-when criteria of spec, test-strategy and plan (loop_contract.stage_exit called for each covered stage; +564 B, 310 for spec and 254 for test-strategy, on the 9,216 B contract budget [M]); (2) the covered documents are listed by the script in the child's scope from STAGE_FILES (the opening can name several files but nothing binds or checks them; the host-written scope can silently narrow); (3) the Improve prompt and the stage references are composed from the covered stages, not tripled; (4) PLANNING_REVIEW_FOCUS gains one generic cross-document clause; (5) a covered stage's accepted record cannot be amended (the child's final_result is canonicalised as plan), so a changed decision is made in the files, the revised files go in evidence_refs and the summary states the change; (6) the commit gate needs no change, because improve_changes snapshots the whole Git tree at improve-bind [I, from two reports].
modes.schedule: Children for a two-item run: plan (covering spec, test-strategy, plan), step-plan W1, test-spec W1, step-plan W2, test-spec W2, carry-forward, system-test-author, release-plan = 8; three in the planning window [M, my scratch walk]. The plan child starts when the plan result is accepted, which is the last point before prepare, so improve-reconcile (legal only at the bound plan child before prepare, _reconciliation_permitted [M]) keeps its route. It reviews the union of STAGE_FILES for spec, test-strategy and plan: living spec.md and feature spec.md, test-strategy.md, feature plan.md, README.md. A step-plan child reviews the feature plan.md and its step plan; a test-spec child reviews test-spec.md, as in stage.
modes.packet_text: spec: 'Improve: no Improve child starts after this result; the Improve child that starts at plan reviews it together with the test strategy and the plan. If work cannot continue, submit outcome blocked with a truthful summary; when the run stops blocked, the next packet prints its Resume command.' test-strategy: the same with 'the spec' in place of 'the test strategy'. plan: 'Improve: Every plan result, including blocked and repeat, starts this action's Improve child. It is this run's one review of the planning documents: it also covers the accepted spec and test-strategy results, which ShipLoop lists in its packet.' Plus a script-written block in the plan child's packet: 'This child also covers these accepted results, which advanced without their own review; ShipLoop froze their documents into this child's scope and their done-when criteria into its exit condition, so do not restate them in the opening: - spec: <accepted result locator>; documents <paths> - test-strategy: <accepted result locator>; documents <paths>. Review the three results together and against each other: a criterion with no check, a check that needs a file, module or fixture that no step or earlier work creates, two statements that contradict. A covered result's accepted record cannot be amended: change a decision in the files, commit it, name the revised files in evidence_refs and state the change in this result's summary.' step-plan, test-spec and every other stage: unchanged.
modes.expected_minutes: Unknown; no such run exists. Grok medium: lower bound 39.2 min (72.7 minus the three global children's 33.5, if the merged child cost nothing), upper bound 72.7; so once cannot reach 30 whatever the merged child costs [M arithmetic]. A scenario range of about 59-66 min rests on an assumed pass count for the merged child [I, one report]. Luna xhigh: lower bound 213.4 min (375.9 minus 162.5), upper 375.9; the ledger's lever L3, a related one-review-at-the-end shape, estimated 118-178 min saved [I, ledger]; a bottom-up floor from the removed openings and clean passes saves about 30 min [I, one report]. The pass count and minutes of a merged child are unmeasured.

modes.semantics: No model-run Improve child at spec, test-strategy, plan, step-plan or test-spec. Each result is accepted on ShipLoop's own checks at complete and the graph advances directly, as at intake or prepare. The carry-forward, system-test-author and release-plan children keep running. The plan child's stopped-child reconciliation (improve-reconcile) and the plan-time experiments it hosts do not exist: no code path produces a reconcile without the bound plan child [M]. The plan's assumption list is still checked at complete by _check_submitted_assumptions [M]. Spec and test-strategy are committed to docs/shiploop at their own accept, before any review [M, knowledge_home.commit runs after every accepted stage that changed the home].
modes.schedule: Children for a two-item run: carry-forward (last item), system-test-author, release-plan = 3; none in the planning window [M, my scratch walk]. Nothing reviews the five planning documents at planning time.
modes.packet_text: At each of the five stages: 'Improve: no Improve child runs after this result in this run (planning_review: none), so nothing reviews it before the graph advances. Before you call it done, confirm each Done-when condition against the files you wrote, after your last edit. If work cannot continue, submit outcome blocked with a truthful summary; when the run stops blocked, the next packet prints its Resume command.' The plan packet's purpose line reads '... explicit readiness, completion and integration ownership; before you call it done, confirm the evidence supports it.' and the two lines 'Planning experiments guide' and 'Planning investigation notebook' are not printed (they belong to the plan child). The mode-neutral sentences, printed in every mode: COMMON: 'The packet's Improve line says whether this result gets an actual Improve-skill handoff; every result without one is accepted on this step's own checks and the graph advances directly.' Plan duty: 'After creating the initial steps, submit this producer result. The packet's Improve line says whether an Improve child reviews it; until the result is accepted the plan remains a draft and dependent work waits. Link the created plan and any execution graph in evidence_refs so a reviewer can read their actual contents. Do not schedule an extra review stage or claim a review ran.' Step-plan duty (three places): 'Before the steps and graph are used for execution, the Improve child the packet's Improve line names reviews them, when this run has one.' Test-spec duty: 'Any review is the Improve child the packet's Improve line names, immediately after this producer result and before implementation. Do not schedule a review stage or claim it ran.' Test-facility handoff: 'any Improve child's context/notes'.
modes.expected_minutes: Grok medium: 30.3 min by arithmetic (72.7 minus the 42.4 child clock); 26.8 on the exporter's per-stage Improve minutes (45.88 in run-doc-grok-medium-v1210.json [M]); 24.1 on a producer-result-to-receipt clock [I, one report]. This is the gross upper bound on saving, so it sits at the ceiling, not under it. If first-pass review work moves into the producers, add up to the five children's pass-1 minutes (13.3, [I, one report]), giving about 44 at worst; the shifted share is unmeasured. Luna xhigh: 172.5 min by arithmetic (375.9 minus 203.4); worst case about 247 if all 74.4 min of pass-1 time moved to authoring (the share is unmeasured [M for 74.4, ledger F4]). The ledger's floor with no model-run Improve and no Backchain loop beyond the draft is 115-131 min [I], so no review value reaches 30 on Luna xhigh; that needs other levers (L13 backchain none 22-57 min, L11 script lint 35-55, effort), outside this change. Sonnet 5.5: planning already takes 3-5 min and its reviews were 0.0-0.3 min each in the hello runs [I, one report]; the option changes nothing worth measuring there.

engine_changes:
All symbols read in the source tree d1cca62f (ShipLoop 0.53.1). I confirmed the schedule logic on a throwaway scratch copy (about 20 lines in shiploop_stage_spec.py and 6 in shiploop_navigator.py): a two-item walk started 10, 8 and 3 children for stage, once and none (5, 3 and 0 in the planning window); validation refused a missing plan record under once and a missing system-test-author record under none, and accepted a missing spec record under once and a missing plan record under none [M].

I1, option plumbing (no schedule change). shiploop_stage_spec.py: PLANNING_REVIEW_MODES = ('stage','once','none'), DEFAULT_PLANNING_REVIEW (stage until I5). shiploop_navigator.py: add 'planning_review' to _STATE_KEYS; new_state(..., planning_review=DEFAULT_PLANNING_REVIEW) with _need(planning_review in PLANNING_REVIEW_MODES, 'planning review must be one of ...') and state['planning_review']; _validate_current_state: _need(state['planning_review'] in PLANNING_REVIEW_MODES, 'unsupported planning review option; expected one of ...'); recorded_planning_review(state) and its __all__ entry; re-export PLANNING_REVIEW_MODES and DEFAULT_PLANNING_REVIEW. shiploop_protocol.py: --planning-review choices=navigator.PLANNING_REVIEW_MODES on the workspace-start parser and the init parser, the passthrough from workspace start to init, _require_retry_planning_review at both retry sites, planning_review=args.planning_review or DEFAULT in the new_state call. shiploop_navigator_dry_run.py: run_scenario(..., planning_review=) and graph-dry-run --planning-review. Saved runs: no code; the generic missing-fields check refuses them with FRESH_RUN_HINT.

I2, none. shiploop_stage_spec.py: PLANNING_CHOICE_STAGES = {spec, test-strategy, plan, step-plan, test-spec}; reviewed_stages(mode) = with_improve('always') for stage, minus FOLDED_INTO_PLAN for once, minus PLANNING_CHOICE_STAGES for none. Do not redefine guidance.PLANNING_REVIEW_STAGES (the seven): STEP_PLANNING_STAGES = PLANNING_REVIEW_STAGES minus planning_revision.PLANNING_STAGES is derived from it at import and drives which packets print accepted spec and plan sources [M]. Leave _IMPROVE_STAGES static (KISS: a record at an unreviewed stage can only come from a hand edit; the required set and the active-child check carry the rule). shiploop_navigator.py: _improve_checkpoint replaces 'stage in guidance.PLANNING_REVIEW_STAGES' with 'stage in stage_spec.reviewed_stages(recorded_planning_review(state))' (it is the only place that decides whether a result parks a child, called by apply and by _validate_current_state); _validate_current_state builds the required set 'planning' from reviewed_stages(mode) instead of the static set, keeping the no-test-stage exclusion (item_scope.no_test_item), and rewords two refusals ('...including every planning-stage result this run's planning_review option reviews'; 'a stage that does not start an Improve child in this run (planning_review: X)'); _improve_line(stage) becomes _improve_line(state, stage) (call site in render) with the none text; the 'Planning phase intent' block: plan purpose and the two experiment lines depend on 'plan' in reviewed_stages(mode). shiploop_prompts.py: COMMON, the plan duty, the three step-plan duty variants (including the _INLINE_DUTY_PARAGRAPHS ones), the test-spec duty and the TEST_FACILITY_HANDOFF replacement become mode-neutral (no planning_review parameter on guidance.prompt: one place, _improve_line, depends on the mode, S-12). shiploop_navigator_dry_run.py: REVIEWED3 and activity() become a per-mode literal table (independent oracle on purpose). skills/shiploop-e2e-audit/harness/dag_replay.py (_PLANNING_CHECKPOINTS literal, _path_steps, synthetic cases that finish a child at spec, test-strategy or step-plan) takes the case's mode; workflow_review.py (imports that literal and marks 'accepted planning-stage result has no Improve record' as unknown and not comparable) reads the recorded mode; both keep a literal second copy on purpose.

I3, test-author probe (independent of the option). shiploop_stage_spec.py: add 'test-probe' to COMPLETE_RUNS and complete_runs=('test-probe',) on the test-author row. shiploop_test_loop.py: PROBE_STAGE, = stage_spec.with_complete_run('test-probe'); stage_commands treats PROBE_STAGE like test-green and test-red (focused commands only); verify judges the probe in red mode and accepts the statuses red and green (a test ran), refusing no-tests, not-red, ids-missing and uncounted; _explain names the placeholder rule for those statuses at the probe; record['expect']. shiploop_navigator.py: _test_probe_gate beside _test_red_gate, called from the dispatch complete branch (cursor_stage == test_loop.PROBE_STAGE), on a done result only. shiploop_prompts.py: one generic sentence in the test-author text and one in the step-plan text (S-8: no language-specific wording).

I4, once. loop_contract.stage_exit stays per stage; improve_start_contract appends it for every covered stage (new helper stage_spec.covered_stages(stage, mode): (spec, test-strategy, plan) for plan under once, else (stage,)); the script prepends the covered documents (knowledge_home.STAGE_FILES expanded for the feature) to context.scope; _render_improve prints the covered-results block from state and history; guidance._improve_prompt and the stage-reference printing take the covered stages (plan's close prints 18 reference locators against 12 [I, one report]); IMPROVE_SCOPES['plan'] and PLANNING_REVIEW_FOCUS name three documents and one cross-document clause; _derived_improve_receipt summary names the covered stages; _improve_line prints the once texts; the required set in _validate_current_state follows reviewed_stages('once').

I5, default flip: DEFAULT_PLANNING_REVIEW = 'none' and explicit planning_review='stage' in every fixture that walks the old schedule.

Unchanged: Stage.improve rows, guidance.PLANNING_REVIEW_STAGES, finish_improve, shiploop_standalone_improve binding, _improve_change_gate and improve_changes, knowledge_home, shiploop_assumptions, the vendored Until Loop (test/improve.test.sh pins its hashes).

spec_carve_out:
Own commit first (I0), before any code, like 9747d769. It carries four ride-along edits and one new carve-out. Edit (a), S-10 head: 'Except for the carve-out below, there is no iteration cap' becomes 'Except for the carve-outs below, there is no iteration cap'. Edit (b), end of the 2026-10-04 carve-out: 'Quality, test and Improve loops are not covered; their no-cap rule stands.' becomes 'Quality and test loops are not covered, nor are Improve loops except as the next carve-out says; their no-cap rule stands.' Edit (c), table row 'S-9, S-10' in 'How the harness checks the clauses': 'Improve children' becomes 'Improve children (read against the run's recorded planning_review)'. The existing test_spec_s10_names_its_one_carve_out asserts the singular phrase and must change in the same commit. Edit (d), insert after the 2026-10-04 carve-out and before S-11 (it must come after it: the parity test BackchainPassesOptionTest.test_the_spec_carve_out_names_the_option_the_code_defines splits at the first '**S-10 carve-out' and reads to '**S-11'; the new text names no --backchain-passes flag and no 'defaults to X pass' phrase [M]):

**S-10 carve-out, owner decision 2026-10-05** (anchor: the owner's rule that
planning takes no more than 30 minutes, decided after the evaluation of the
skill-craft 1.21.0 battleship runs on Luna xhigh and Grok medium, not a clause
this serves; it relaxes S-9, S-10 and the rule that a step iterates until a
check confirms each exit criterion, for the Improve review of planning results,
and says so). The run option `planning_review` (state key `planning_review`,
recorded in `state.md` at `init` or `workspace start`, never changed afterwards;
a saved run without it is refused) selects which of the five planning results
`spec`, `test-strategy`, `plan`, `step-plan` and `test-spec` start an Improve
child. `--planning-review stage` starts one after each of the five, as before.
`--planning-review once` starts one after `plan` over the accepted `spec`,
`test-strategy` and `plan` results together, and, as before, one after each
work item's `step-plan` and `test-spec`. `--planning-review none` starts none at
these five. The option defaults to `none`. The Improve children after
`system-test-author` and `release-plan` and the last `carry-forward` start in
every mode; the quality and test loops and the Backchain child are not covered
and their rules stand. Every Improve child that starts is unchanged: a contract
the script writes (in `once` the script, not the model, adds each covered
stage's done-when criteria to the plan child's exit condition and lists the
covered documents in its scope), the same two-review or unchanged-first-pass
exit and no iteration cap, so S-10 holds for each loop that runs. In `none`, and
in `once` for `spec` and `test-strategy` until the plan child ends, a planning
result is accepted without a review loop. What stands in for the loop is what
S-9 can name: the Done-when criteria the packet prints and the producer's duty
to confirm each; ShipLoop's gates at `complete` (cited files exist; the plan's
assumption list; the step plan's commands, criteria, paths and dependency
order; the knowledge home's required files, credential screen and
requirement-ID retention); the structural, record-only `backchain-check`; at
`test-author`, a run of the focused commands that must run tests, so a test
that cannot load is refused where it can be fixed; and then the `test-red`,
`test-green`, `regression` and system-test gates, which ShipLoop runs and
records. No script-run check at planning, in any mode, covers whether the spec's
criteria are complete and verifiable, whether the test strategy maps every
criterion to a check, or whether a test spec's oracles are independent. An
Improve child's own S-9 evidence has been loop mechanics the script counts
(passes, the review streak, a Git cross-check, the commit rule), never a check
of the review's content, so `none` removes a second look, not a script-run
check. In `none` the plan child's stopped-child reconciliation
(`improve-reconcile`) and the plan-time experiments it hosts do not exist; the
plan's assumption list is still checked at `complete`. In `once` a covered
result's accepted record is not amended by the later child: a changed decision
is made in the files and stated in the child's result. Basis: in the Luna xhigh
run the planning window was 375.9 minutes, 203.4 (54%) in five Improve children
(22 passes), and in the Grok medium run 72.7 minutes, 42.4 (58%) in five
children (26 passes); `spec`, `test-strategy` and `plan` took about 80% and 79%
of those; the Luna reviews caught five warranted fixes and did not raise the
`test-red` defect whose redo cost 165.9 minutes. No run without the planning
reviews exists, so the rate of defects that escape without them is unknown.

quality_risk: What the review bought: on Luna xhigh 22 passes gave 5 warranted fixes, 5 minor, 2 corrections and 10 no change (the ledger's labels); on Grok medium 26 passes, 4 passes that fixed a real defect, 6 marginal, 4 churn and 12 no change (one investigation's labels). Warranted findings were almost all in the global documents and fell in classes the later nets also catch but late: weak or missing oracles (JSON content type and error bodies), traceability links, a contradiction between two documents or confirm lines, an untested stated requirement (/api/new recovery), and a regression command naming criteria it cannot confirm. No script check at planning covers these (the existing script gates cover shape, files, the assumption list, commands and criteria, the knowledge home, and structure only). none gives up that second look at planning; once keeps one look at the global documents but after test-strategy and plan were written against an unreviewed spec (cascade cost unmeasured, the accepted records of covered stages stay stale after the review). none also gives up plan reconcile and plan-time experiments (the one measured catch rate for seeded plan-stage platform errors was 0/15 without and 10/15 with the claim bullet [I, one report]) and commits an unreviewed spec into the knowledge later runs inherit. The review missed the defect that cost most: on Luna xhigh a plan that gave the tests no real module to load cost a 165.9-minute redo against 99.2 minutes the first time. The 123-minute 1.16.1 case the brief pairs with it is, in the ledger's own words, an analogue (an implement revise, test code contradicting its own helper), not the same defect [M, ledger F9]; so one same-class event, with review on. Break-even: none saves at most 203.4 min on Luna xhigh against an escape that cost 66.7 min (extra over the first pass) to 165.9 (the whole redo): 1.2 to 3.0 extra escapes per run [I arithmetic]; on Grok medium none saves at most 42.4 min and the cost of an escape was never measured (the probe stopped before test-red), so the break-even is unknown. The escape rate with review off is unknown: no run without planning reviews exists. The default is one constant for every host: on Sonnet 5.5 reviews were 0.0-0.3 min each and changed nothing in the hello runs, so none saves little there and removes a small catch [I, one report]. What carries the exit criterion instead: S-9 holds only structurally. Mechanical parts are carried by script-run gates at complete (cited files exist, assumption list, step-plan commands, criteria, paths and order, knowledge-home files, credential screen and requirement-ID retention), the new test-author probe (carries test-author's own done-when 'each case has a test the focused command runs', which nothing checked before), and later test-red, test-green, regression and system-test runs. The semantic parts (complete and verifiable spec criteria, test-strategy mapping, independent oracles) have no script-run check in any mode; under none they rest on the producer's printed Done-when loop, the later gates and the end-of-work review; under once they are reviewed once after later documents depend on them. This is where the owner's primary rule ('steps iterate until a stated check confirms each exit criterion') and 'enterprise rigour is standard' strain; the carve-out says so. A script-run requirement-ID presence check was considered and not recommended: the one traceability finding I could identify was a wrong link, which an ID-presence check does not catch, and with no ID in the spec the check would pass having run nothing (S-9). I could not read what the Luna traceability finding was, so this is [I].
measurement: Quality first, then tokens, then time (the owner's eval priority); unmeasured is unknown. Baselines: the 1.21.0 Grok medium and Luna xhigh battleship runs, one each, stage times vary about 2x between runs of the same model [M, stage-clock.md]. First run: a Grok medium planning-only probe stopping at the first test-spec accept (as the 1.21.0 probe did) at the default none, repeated once so the variance is visible. Read: (1) planning window and minutes per stage, from timeline.json accepted joined to state.md history, against 72.7; (2) Improve children in the window (expect 0) and Improve minutes elsewhere; (3) authoring minutes per stage, stage minutes minus Improve minutes, against the baseline (spec 4.0, test-strategy 5.5, plan 6.2, step-plan 2.7, test-spec 1.5; about 26.8 for the window [M, run-doc-grok-medium-v1210.json]): growth means first-pass review work moved into authoring; (4) document bytes against the baseline (spec 19,151 B, test-strategy 20,880 B, test-spec 11,162 B [M, run doc]); (5) planning_review recorded in state.md. Then let a second probe run on to green (the Grok baseline stopped at test-spec, so this needs the owner's go) and read: whether the test-author probe fired and what it said, test-red outcomes, revise count and minutes, and which defect classes reach test-red, test-green, regression or system test that the baseline review caught (oracle strength, contradiction, missing coverage). A stage control cell is needed for any comparison to green: the harness has no way to pass --planning-review (owner decision), so until then the 1.21.0 runs are the only controls. Luna xhigh: one run at none, planning window and the W1 test-red outcome. For once, once built: passes and minutes of the merged child against 33.5 min and 20 passes (Grok) and 162.5 min and 17 passes (Luna), improve-start refusals for size, any improve-reconcile. Revert criteria (comparisons, no invented numbers): (a) if the Grok medium none window is not under the owner's 30 minutes, the review change has done what it can and the remaining minutes are authoring and Backchain, so the rule says rethink planning; this is not by itself a revert; (b) revert the default to stage (one constant, one pin) if none is not faster to green than a stage control on the same cell, if escaped defects or revises appear that the baseline review caught, or if a verdict that passes on the same cell at stage fails; (c) for once, revert it as the default if the merged child costs at least as many minutes as the three children it replaced or an improve-start size refusal recurs. Do not claim the 30-minute target is met from a window alone.
owner_decisions: Default value. Recommended: none, the only value whose arithmetic lands at the ceiling on Grok medium (24.1-30.3 min gross, possibly up to about 44 if first-pass review work moves into authoring), at the cost of all model-run review at the five planning stages. once cannot meet the ceiling (at least 39.2 min). If you choose once the carve-out sentence and one constant change, and planning stays over 30 on both measured models. Either way Luna xhigh does not reach 30 from this change.

A child bound to test-spec cannot amend the step plan's steps, test_commands, criteria or paths, so a structural fix becomes a revise and a re-authoring pass (the Luna redo's step-plan took 120.1 min against 38.7), and it would save only the test-spec child (2.5-3.0 min on Grok, 14.2 on Luna).

The opening allowance of the once plan child: the host-writable opening is 4.2-4.4 KB today and about 3.6-3.9 KB with the three-stage exit [I, two reports; the 564 B added is [M]]; whether a real battleship-size opening fits is unmeasured. The earlier refusals for size cost minutes.

Run-to-run variance: stage times vary about 2x between runs of the same model; a single probe cannot show a small effect, though removing 54-58% of the window is large against it.

The test footprint at the flip: three prototypes measured 116-142 tests in 11-22 files for a once default and 187 tests in 20 files for a none default on a 36-file subset [I, from reports]; the chain, workspace, keepalive, lint, run-review and e2e suites were not all run on any prototype, and the dry-run file aborted early, so these are lower bounds.

I did not run the repository's full suites against my scratch prototype, only a schedule walk and a state validation; the other evidence for the engine claims is from my read of the code and from four investigation reports whose figures I re-checked against the evidence directory where I cite [M].
guard_for_the_missing_module: Yes, a cheap script-run guard exists: a test-author probe, increment I3, independent of the option and required before the default flips. Why the existing gate did not help [M]: the test-red gate (_test_red_gate, called from the dispatch complete branch) returns immediately unless the submitted outcome is done, and the Luna host sent revise at test-red ('the focused command was not run because it would fail during import; test-red forbids product-code edits'); the gate never ran. Nothing owned the missing module: test-red says 'Do not edit product code', and its not-red refusal tells the host to 'fix the test setup', with no owner for a loadable seam; test-author's own done-when ('each case in the test spec has a test the focused command runs') had no script check because the row has no complete_runs. One investigation fed a real Node test-runner missing-module output to the real judge: red mode returns ids-missing (IDs listed) or uncounted (none), so the check would have refused had the gate run [I, reported]. The guard: add 'test-probe' to stage_spec.COMPLETE_RUNS and complete_runs=('test-probe',) on the test-author row; in shiploop_test_loop add PROBE_STAGE, make stage_commands return the focused commands for it, and make verify judge it in red mode accepting red and green (a test ran) and refusing no-tests, not-red, ids-missing and uncounted, with _explain naming the placeholder rule; in shiploop_navigator add _test_probe_gate beside _test_red_gate in the dispatch complete branch (done results only, same MAX_REFUSED_RUNS, remedy revise through the existing _remedy table); two generic sentences in the test-author and step-plan prompts. Cost: one focused-command run at test-author's done, seconds, the same path as test-red [I]. The refusal comes at test-author, where creating the minimal loadable placeholder is allowed (edits are not script-enforced and scope_refusal tolerates it [M]). Tests go through the real gate: refusal on a recorded missing-module output, acceptance after the placeholder, red and green accepted, no-command items accepted, revise accepted after MAX_REFUSED_RUNS. Saving if it had existed: up to the 165.9-minute redo on Luna xhigh, less a few minutes [I]. It protects run total, not the planning window. Not covered: a test that contradicts its own helper (the 1.16.1 implement revise) looks RED at test-red. Rejected alternatives: static import analysis (language-specific, S-8), a Backchain consumer (the graph models implement steps only), lint (needs a configured resolver), text alone (Luna's reviews and host ignored text of this kind), and gating revise at test-red on a ShipLoop run (the host can still only revise, the costly route). Lives in: shiploop_stage_spec.py, shiploop_test_loop.py, shiploop_navigator.py, shiploop_prompts.py.
